stem: A test planned for 14 days ends with p = 0.09. The manager says: "Let's run it one more week and see if it gets below 0.05." What is the problem?

options.text: There is none: more data always makes the result of a test more trustworthy
Extending until it becomes significant is peeking and inflates false positives
p = 0.09 already counts as significant at the 10% level, so the test can ship now
The extra week is fine as long as nobody looks at the result before it ends
